P1.evidence: P1a not applicable — no setter pre-qualified this lead and there were no notes to read back. P1b partial: he set a purpose frame but not the four-part one, and he did it well under pressure — the prospect opened by asking where to buy kettlebells and the rep declined to be pulled into logistics: "Before we go and buy any kettlebells, let's just have a conversation and actually find out if this is right fit for you working with Trevor." That covers what you need and implicitly what is in the way, but not where you are or where you want to go. P1c hit — he asked for agreement ("Right?") and got "All right. Yes." P1d hit and well phrased: "If you could just walk me through what's been going on. What's the main thing you're trying to fix right now in terms of fitness, health, in general?"

P2.evidence: P2a miss — age 63 was volunteered in the opening answer and never asked; height and weight were never established at all, despite fat loss being the prospect's stated goal. P2b hit: "in terms of, like, what do you do on a daily basis? Like, do you move around, or your job is..." P2c is the critical miss. Health conditions, own or hereditary, were never asked. Both of the conditions that should have changed this entire call — a single kidney with a protein restriction, and rheumatoid arthritis — arrived unprompted, the kidney as an aside during a diet answer and the arthritis immediately after the rep had already accepted "No. I'm good. I'm good. Yes, nothing." P2d hit, and the follow-up was genuinely good: "When you move a lot, does it appear somewhere else in your body?" surfaced the knee. P2e partial — established he had restarted two weeks earlier and was doing classic strength work, but never established actual days trained. P2f miss. P2g hit: "So brief me in, what's your menu during the week?" P2h miss — sleep never raised once, on a call where the prospect disclosed a six-month depressive episode. P2i miss — energy never asked, and when the prospect volunteered "I don't have the energy to work out the way I want to" at 00:33:38 it was absorbed into a rapport story rather than explored.

P3.evidence: Effortful but it never landed. P3a partial and leading — "For you, it's not the aesthetics side of things, right?" put the answer in the prospect's mouth and he pushed back: "No, of course. Who doesn't want to look good?" P3c hit and was the best moment of the phase: "Is there anything else that you've been putting off... Maybe some sports?" produced kitesurfing, and the rep correctly challenged the self-disqualification with "Why would you say you won't do it?" P3e hit and asked three separate times. But the prospect could not or would not go deeper — "I don't know what to say", "I don't know. Life, my life's going to change" — and the rep responded by pressing and then by dismissing the answer: "So when you say like, nothing will change, that's silly." P3f and P3g are the real failure. A wife who "doesn't understand why I have these ups and downs", a daughter getting married this year, and parents he had just spent six months caring for were all on the table, and not one of them was asked about. The rep drove the impact question to work stress and generic life improvement instead, so the deep why never got past the prospect's own framing of exercise as medication.

P4.evidence: P4c is a clean hit and the best question on the call: "Why didn't you go back to what you were doing?" produced the honest answer — "Because I was overseas for many different reasons and I was also depressed and I just didn't get motivated. And then I was a little injured so I was trying to give an excuse." The rep then handled the disclosure well: "That's a powerful word to use, depressed." P4a and P4b partial — CrossFit, gym, bodyweight and the two overload injuries all emerged, but volunteered rather than asked for. P4e and P4f were never run, so the prospect never named his own structural gap and was never asked why he cannot do it alone. That question was unusually available here: he has twice injured himself training unsupervised, once for a full year, and he said so out loud.

P5.evidence: P5a hit, at a one-year rather than two-year horizon: "if nothing changes, and you would be sitting a year from now, not exercising, how would that actually affect you?" The answer was the most powerful thing said on the call — "Oh, I'm going to be depressed." The rep then closed it down in a single line, "We don't want to get there, yeah?", took the "No", and immediately pivoted to the upside: "But on the other side, there's always the flip side." There was no settle test, no "why not", and no line in the sand. He had a 63-year-old with documented six-month strength decline, rheumatoid arthritis and a stated link between inactivity and depression, and he had just been handed the cost of inaction in the prospect's own words. Abandoning it there is the single largest process failure on this call and it is why the later timing objection had nothing to push against.

P6.evidence: P6a never asked — the belief question about getting there with the right structure and the right person in his corner was skipped entirely. P6b partial: "Are you fully committed to showing up and doing this for yourself to become that better version of Caesar that depression is gone?" is a commitment ask but not the go-all-in question, and it was asked with the price already flagged as the next topic. P6c is a clear miss and the decisive one. The answer he received was "Andrew, the answer is yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, yes. I just don't know if I can afford the program." That is not a clear yes, it is a yes with a money objection attached, delivered before any number had been named. The script says to return to Phase 5 on hesitation. Instead he said "Yeah, let's talk about it" and named $6,000 into an open, unisolated affordability doubt.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted but declined, so payment and onboarding were never reachable and the phase drops out of the denominator.

objection_plays.detail: Two triggers, one before the price ("I just don't know if I can afford the program", 00:41:55) and one after ("I wasn't expecting this amount", 00:42:16). The pre-price trigger was ignored entirely — that was the moment to run the isolation move, and instead he proceeded to the number. Post-price he ran a partial version of the break-it-up move twice: "But is it that you cannot cover it like up front?", "We have ways that we can structure the...", and "Even if it was structured in a way that it wouldn't have to be in one sitting, the payment." Everything else in the play was skipped. He never isolated with "finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%", never used the SHOULD I versus HOW reframe, never asked permission for an open financial conversation, and ran none of the six financial-picture items — no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards, no available credit, no investments. He also never put an actual structure on the table, only the idea of one, so the prospect was declining an abstraction rather than a plan.

Explicit trigger: "I have my daughter's wedding this year, so it's really not the right time for me" and "year, after January. Right now I cannot do anything." Not one OD move was run. No "are you ever going to have another busy season", no "things never slow down, when does it actually become the right time", no "the longer you wait the harder this gets", no "the only thing you can control is right now". The metabolism-and-injuries-compound move was better supported here than on any other call in this batch, and by facts the prospect had supplied himself: he is 63, he lost 45 seconds of handstand hold in six months, he has rheumatoid arthritis taking his grip, and injuries now cost him up to a year. Waiting until January is measurably more expensive for this man than for anyone else in the batch, and none of it was said. The rep conceded in one line — "Cool, man. Look... Sure thing. No worries at all."

Clinical fit. The prospect has a single kidney with a stated protein restriction and rheumatoid arthritis with progressive grip loss. Neither is answerable by any scripted play, and the script has no clinical path at all — the same gap already logged from the Tyron Giuliani call. Here it is worse than a missing rebuttal: the absence of a clinical route meant the rep presented a generic high-protein, meat-and-eggs recommendation and a grip-dependent load-progression guarantee to a prospect for whom both are contraindicated or unachievable. This is a script gap that creates risk rather than merely losing deals, and it should be read alongside the flags file.
No deliberation objection. The prospect made a decision on the call rather than asking for time to think.
A wife is mentioned but never as a decision-maker or consult requirement.
The opposite of fear or doubt. The prospect volunteered strong trust without being asked: "seeing Trevor on his videos, I believe in him. Even though there is AI... I trust him, okay? I trust him."

notes: Two coachable failures and one that is bigger than coaching. Process: the consequence frame produced "Oh, I'm going to be depressed" and the rep dropped it in one line to go to the upside, then named $6,000 into an affordability doubt the prospect had already voiced and that was never isolated. Run P5b-d on that answer and isolate before pricing and this call is at least still alive. The OD play was fully triggered and entirely unrun, on the one prospect in the batch for whom the cost-of-waiting argument is factually strongest. Beyond process: health conditions were never asked (P2c), and the two that were volunteered — a single kidney and rheumatoid arthritis — were then contradicted by the nutrition advice and by the guarantee respectively. See the flags file; this is not a scoring issue.
